newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Blue Circle heats up its profit. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Blue Circle heats up its profit. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]

text.p: Blue Circle Industries Plc reported a nine percent rise in pretax profits on Monday, underpinned by a rebound at its heating division.

The British-based building materials group remained cautious on the timing of a recovery in French and German markets and it also warned about the impact of the pound's strength. (Corrects to clarify that pound's strength is a separate factor)
Pretax profits were 297.6 million pounds ($477 million) versus 272.8 million in 1995, while total sales grew to 1.81 billion against 1.77 billion. The dividend was raised to 13.25 pence from 12.5.
Group chief executive Keith Orrell-Jones said the company "performed very well...despite difficult trading conditions in the UK and mainland Europe."
Commenting on the outlook, Orrell-Jones said: "This year we expect the heating improvement to continue and steady progress in the existing heavy building materials businesses."

BCI shares fell in early trading even though analysts said the results were broadly positive and in line with market forecasts. At 1055 GMT, the shares stood at 394 pence, down 21 1/2 pence from Friday's close.

"The results seem to be very much in line. The Canadian deal seem to be done at a good price and the outlook for the current year is good, so it stays a 'buy' as far as we're concerned," UBS analyst Simon Brown said in reference to the company's current acquisition of Canada's St Mary's Cement.

The company said the 164 million pound acquisition of the building materials company was expected to be earnings enhancing within the first year of ownership, with completion of the deal expected by April.
Another UBS analyst, Mark Hake, said he knew of no reason for the share fall before the company met analysts.
"The results were in line, the meeting itself was upbeat. Blue Circle backed up the logic for the St Mary cement acquisition," he said and called the outook for the group positive.

Despite progress made in 1996, finance director James Loudon said it was still unclear when the French and German markets would recover and also issued a warning shot on the impact of sterling strength this year.
"Sterling had a minor impact in 1996. But this year may be a different story. If sterling remains at this level it will wipe five to 10 million off profits before tax," he said in an interview.
Blue Circle is the latest British exporter to suffer from the rise in the value of the pound against the mark and dollar.

Looking at a divisional breakdown, heavy building materials profits were 244.3 million versus 241.5 million. Heating profits jumped to 35 million from 17.1 million, but bathroom profits fell to 24.6 million from 27 million.

Blue Circle cited the sound performance of heavy building materials in the U.S. and Malaysia in particular and added that the heating division had completed the first phase of its restructuring which saw 900 jobs go out of planned cuts of 1,000-1,400.
Current trading has seen continued growth in the boiler market.
"In the UK we have seen boiler demand pick up by 10-11 percent last year which has continued into 1997."

Heavy building materials remained ahead in 1996, apart from Britain and Chile. Britain suffered a four percent slide in cement demand last year, but the market has recovered two percent this year and is seen continuing to improve.
Chile saw cement prices soften, Loudon said.
"But that business is still making extremely good returns on capital employed. Prices in Chile could soften a little and will probably stabilise, but we're doubtful of any kind of price increase."

The group plans to maintain a programme of heavy capital expenditure over the next five years of one billion pounds, he said, but still had the financial capacity to make acquisitions where necessary.
Blue Circle is eyeing the U.S., India, Argentina, Indonesia and Thailand heavy material markets in particular. ($ = 0.623 British Pounds)
